sourceText:
In case as mentioned the sensitivity test was performed successfully:” Sensibility test has been performed with success during HV test so we could think that it won’t be necessary to install the PDC as initially planned.” Then perhaps it will be not necessary to install the “forgotten” additional sensor.

The point is at which condition the mentioned sensitivity test has been performed. Important is to perform the test with the signal level which has been defined during the STEP 1 Sensitivity test, see attached report : R47.00882-PE. So according to the given report for F35-41, it shall be 5V. The value of 5V we declare for GIS of F35-41 and F35-41g the mentioned report is attached normally to the tender or is handed over to the customer in the project phase. Without that document the proper HV test with UHF PD measurement is practically impossible.

In case you see the 5V signal between two sensors than one can conclude the clearance between the sensors is sufficient and in that case one sensor can be omitted. 

Your request is showing no SLD, no positions of sensors, no signal amplitudes, no test conditions, no type of calibrator (we use PDx CAL2B). So frankly speaking not enough details to answer the question seriously. The recommendations from SEH are created to be able measure the signal which is generated by the possible defects. The UHF sensor allows monitoring and the tests onside even without coupling capacitors. 

My private opinion on UHF sensors is eighter to install the sensor properly and to be able to measure or not install them at all.
Too many signals detected are as well not good and can lead to false positive results of monitoring and at the end increase the uncertainty of the customer for our products.
